verdict.root_cause: cartservice is in a startup crash loop because it cannot establish a connection to its Redis cart backend, and the only recorded mutation in the window is an automated environment-configuration edit at 04:19:22 that set the cart Redis address to a redis-cart endpoint on port 6380 (tr_5b25114cf774). cartservice was logging clean cart operations at ~04:12 and by 04:22 is repeatedly timing out after 15-40s against exactly that host:port and dying on an unhandled exception in the Redis connection-establishment path called from Main (tr_6918adff1097). Because the process never reaches a serving state, checkoutservice's outbound hipstershop.CartService/GetCart call fails fast (0.4-1.1ms) with no cartservice server-side span at all, aborting PlaceOrder before shipping/payment/currency/email are ever reached, and the error status propagates up through checkoutservice to frontend (tr_35d30c8d5982, tr_85399cf58a71). The absence of any cartservice span-metric series - numerator and denominator both missing - is consistent with a service that is not serving rather than a service with a zero error rate (tr_0158ce317070). The proximate trigger is therefore a bad cache-endpoint configuration pushed by platform-automation, not a deploy: no deploy, flag flip, or downstream change is recorded anywhere in the queried window (tr_dd850a819de0, tr_5b25114cf774).
verdict.reasoning: Four independent lines converge on cartservice's Redis connection as the origin and on the 04:19:22 config edit as the trigger. (1) Causal direction: the trace evidence puts the deepest error-bearing span on checkoutservice's outbound GetCart with no cartservice server span, which locates the fault at or beyond the unmeasured edge into cartservice and explicitly rules out frontend, checkoutservice logic, and every later checkout dependency as originators (tr_35d30c8d5982). (2) Mechanism: cartservice logs name a single dependency - the cart Redis host on port 6380 - failing during initialization from Main, with the process crash-looping rather than degrading, which explains both the missing server spans and the fast-fail shape rather than timeout-shaped latency (tr_6918adff1097, tr_35d30c8d5982). (3) Trigger: the only change on record anywhere in scope is the automated edit setting that exact Redis address, in the exact dependency class the crash names (tr_5b25114cf774), while frontend/checkout/downstream change logs are empty (tr_dd850a819de0). (4) Timing: cartservice was healthy at ~04:12, the config landed at 04:19:22, alerts fired at 04:22, and frontend's error ratio has a zero floor inside the window - an onset, not a carried-in baseline (tr_6918adff1097, tr_85399cf58a71). The missing cartservice metric series is a measurement gap, not health, and the corpus case cart-bad-image-tag is a direct warning against reading flat/absent cart error metrics as evidence the cart tier is fine. That said, this is a correlation in time plus a matching dependency name - no specialist verified that 6380 is the wrong port or that a listener exists on the previous value, which is why I do not rate this high.
open_questions: Was port 6380 itself the defect (e.g. the correct endpoint being 6379, or TLS expected on 6380 while the client logs abortConnect/TLS off), or is the address correct and redis-cart itself down or unreachable? No one queried the Redis backend's health, listeners, or network path.

The change record shows 'no prior value recorded' - it is unresolved whether this was a first-time introduction of the variable, a change from a working value, or a change-log gap. Without the prior value a revert target cannot be named with certainty.

The 03:50-04:12 interval of the triage window was never queried by any specialist; three separate findings flag this gap. If frontend or cart errors were already present before 04:19, the config edit could be a reaction to the incident rather than its cause.

Why do cartservice span metrics have no denominator at all across 04:12-04:27? Crash-looping explains it, but a renamed service_name label or a broken span-metrics pipeline would produce the same emptiness and would change how much weight the metric absence carries.

The 4 unmeasured edges crossed by triage are not all accounted for; only the checkout->cart edge was characterised. Whether any other unmeasured edge is contributing to the 12-service blast radius is unestablished.
Restart counts, OOM/CPU pressure, and container-runtime status for cartservice were never retrieved, so a resource-exhaustion contributor alongside the config change cannot be formally excluded.
